title: Electrical & Electronics Fundamentals
subtitle: Voltage, current, resistance and power; Ohm's and Kirchhoff's laws; and working safely with electricity.
outcomes: Explain charge, voltage, current and resistance
Calculate circuits with Ohm's law and power formulas
Analyse series, parallel and divider circuits with Kirchhoff's laws

toc.text: Voltage and current in a practical circuit
How voltage, current, and resistance relate

pool.q: What are the three fundamental particles that make up most atoms?
pool.explain: Protons and neutrons are tightly bound in the nucleus; electrons can move.
pool.evidence: are called protons , neutrons and electrons

pool.q: What is the elementary charge?
options: The charge of a full battery
The charge of a whole atom
The charge of one electron, the smallest known carrier of charge
pool.explain: All electric charge comes in multiples of it.
pool.evidence: Being that one electron is the smallest known carrier of electric charge, this last figure of charge for the electron is defined as the elementary charge

pool.q: What distinguishes conductors from insulators?
options: Conductors are always metal; insulators are always plastic
Conductors have high electron mobility (many free electrons); insulators have low mobility
Insulators carry more current than conductors
Conductors store charge; insulators release it
pool.explain: Dirty water and concrete conduct too, but far less well than metals.
pool.evidence: Materials with high electron mobility (many free electrons) are called conductors

pool.q: Why is voltage always referenced between two points?
options: Because current flows in two directions
Because voltage is an expression of potential energy between two levels
pool.explain: Like a mass that could drop from one height to another, voltage is relative.
pool.evidence: Because voltage is an expression of potential energy, representing the possibility or potential for energy release as the electrons move from one "level" to another, it is always referenced between two points.

pool.q: What is an open circuit?
options: A break in the continuity of the circuit prevents current throughout
A circuit with very low resistance
A circuit with the switch closed
pool.explain: Reconnecting the break makes it a closed circuit again.
pool.evidence: where a break in the continuity of the circuit prevents current throughout

pool.q: Why is a short circuit dangerous?
options: The current can become very large, releasing energy dramatically, usually as heat
Resistance increases until the wire melts
pool.explain: With almost no resistance, current is limited only by the source.
pool.evidence: the magnitude of electric current may be very large in such a short circuit

pool.q: Who most often uses electron flow notation?
options: Introductory textbooks and scientists such as solid-state physicists
pool.explain: Many engineers use conventional flow, from positive to negative, instead.
pool.evidence: Electron flow is most often seen in introductory textbooks (this one included) and in the writings of professional scientists, especially solid-state physicists

pool.q: What is electric current?
options: The potential energy between two points
The continuous movement of free electrons through the conductors of a circuit
The opposition to the flow of electrons
The heat produced by a resistor
pool.explain: Ohm's law links current (I), voltage (E) and resistance (R).
pool.evidence: This continuous movement of free electrons through the conductors of a circuit is called a current

pool.q: What is power?
options: The total amount of work done
A measure of how rapidly a standard amount of work is done
pool.explain: In electric circuits power is measured in watts.
pool.evidence: Power is a measure of how rapidly a standard amount of work is done.

pool.q: Does voltage or current on its own constitute power?
pool.explain: Power depends on both voltage and current together (P = IE).
pool.evidence: It must be understood that neither voltage nor current by themselves constitute power.

pool.q: What are resistors made for?
options: Creating a precise quantity of resistance to insert into a circuit
pool.explain: Variable resistors add a shaft or lever to adjust the resistance.
pool.evidence: Special components called resistors are made for the express purpose of creating a precise quantity of resistance for insertion into a circuit.

pool.q: How does the resistance of almost all metals behave?
options: It falls to zero in sunlight
pool.explain: So the resistance of wires is not perfectly constant.
pool.evidence: The phenomenon of resistance changing with variations in temperature is one shared by almost all metals, of which most wires are made.

pool.q: How does varistor breakdown differ from the breakdown of an insulator?
options: It is repeatable — designed to survive repeated breakdowns
pool.explain: A solid insulator often never recovers after high-voltage breakdown.
pool.evidence: Unlike the breakdown of an insulator, varistor breakdown is repeatable: that is, it is designed to withstand repeated breakdowns without failure.

pool.q: Why can you lengthen or shorten connecting wires without changing a circuit's function?
options: Longer wires always add useful resistance
Connecting wires barely affect the circuit, so their length doesn't matter
Circuits only work with short wires
pool.explain: Points joined by wire are electrically common.
pool.evidence: shortening or lengthening the wires as desired without appreciably impacting the circuit's function

pool.q: Why are wires joining common points often given the same label?
options: Common points show the same voltage and resistance measurements
They are always the same colour
pool.explain: Same label, same electrical point.
pool.evidence: Because common points in a circuit will exhibit the same relative voltage and resistance measurements, wires connecting common points are often labeled with the same designation.

pool.q: How does the SPICE program simulate a circuit?
options: From a photo of the circuit
From a text listing that describes the circuit
pool.explain: It outputs the results of its analysis as text too.
pool.evidence: which works by describing a circuit to the computer by means of a listing of text

pool.q: In electric shock, what is tetanus?
pool.explain: It can stop a victim letting go of a live conductor.
pool.evidence: this condition of involuntary muscle contraction is called tetanus

pool.q: What is fibrillation?
options: When scrambled nerve signals stop the heart beating properly
pool.explain: Even currents too low to cause tetanus can cause it.
pool.evidence: scramble nerve cell signals enough that the heart cannot beat properly, sending the heart into a condition known as fibrillation

pool.q: What is an intentional grounding point in a circuit meant to ensure?
options: That one side of the circuit is safe to come in contact with
That the circuit uses less power
pool.explain: The grounded side is electrically common with the earth.
pool.evidence: the presence of an intentional "grounding" point in an electric circuit is intended to ensure that one side of it is safe to come in contact with.

pool.q: What determines how much voltage is dangerous?
options: Only the colour of the wires
Whether the current is AC or DC alone
How much total resistance is in the circuit to oppose the flow of electrons
The brand of the power supply
pool.explain: Current through the body causes harm, and current depends on voltage and resistance.
pool.evidence: Just how much voltage is dangerous depends on how much total resistance is in the circuit to oppose the flow of electrons.

pool.q: Which of these affects the body's electrical resistance?
pool.explain: The contact points on the skin also matter.
pool.evidence: body hydration is another factor impacting the body's electrical resistance

pool.q: What is a circuit secured with all its energy removed said to be in?
pool.explain: Even idle voltage has the potential to harm and must be neutralised.
pool.evidence: securing a circuit, device, or system in this condition is commonly known as placing it in a Zero Energy State

pool.q: What does locking out a disconnect switch protect against?
options: Someone switching it back on while people are still touching the load
pool.explain: This is the purpose of Lock-out/Tag-out.
pool.evidence: protection against the possibility of the disconnect switch being closed

pool.q: Above roughly what voltage is considered potentially dangerous?
pool.explain: Even telephone lines (48 V DC, 150 V AC ringing) exceed it.
pool.evidence: remember that any voltage over 30 is considered potentially dangerous!

pool.q: What are double-insulated appliances?
options: Appliances whose insulating case adds a second layer of insulation
pool.explain: The case adds protection beyond the conductors' own insulation.
pool.evidence: since the insulating case serves as a second layer of insulation above and beyond that of the conductors themselves

pool.q: Why must you never cut the third prong off a power plug?
options: It is the safety ground connection
It only holds the plug in place
pool.explain: Without it, a fault can make a metal case live.
pool.evidence: This is why its so important never to cut the third prong off a power plug

pool.q: Which shock current path through the body is the most dangerous?
options: Finger to finger on one hand
pool.explain: A hand-to-hand path crosses the chest and heart.
pool.evidence: Because a hand-to-hand shock current path is the most dangerous

pool.q: Why must a meter be connected to two points to measure voltage?
options: One lead is only for display
Voltage is always relative between two points
pool.explain: Measuring voltage is a key step in lock-out/tag-out checks.
pool.evidence: Being that voltage is always relative between two points, the meter must be firmly connected to two points in a circuit before it will provide a reliable measurement.

pool.q: Why is lockout/tagout needed during servicing and maintenance?
options: Unexpected start-up or release of stored energy can injure or kill workers
pool.explain: Injuries include electrocution, burns, crushing and amputation.
pool.evidence: During the servicing and maintenance of machines and equipment, the unexpected startup or release of stored energy can result in serious injury or death to workers.

pool.q: What must employers do about hazardous energy control procedures?
options: Train each worker to know, understand and follow them
Use them only for new machines
pool.explain: Retraining keeps workers proficient when methods change.
pool.evidence: Employers are also required to train each worker to ensure that they know, understand, and are able to follow the applicable provisions of the hazardous energy control procedures

pool.q: What is the defining characteristic of a series circuit?
options: There is only one path for electrons to flow
All components share the same two common points
Voltage is equal across every component
pool.explain: In a parallel circuit, all components connect between the same common points instead.
pool.evidence: The defining characteristic of a series circuit is that there is only one path for electrons to flow.

pool.q: What is the defining characteristic of a parallel circuit?
options: All components connect between the same set of electrically common points
There is only one path for electrons
Components are connected end to end
pool.explain: A purely parallel circuit never has more than two sets of common points.
pool.evidence: The defining characteristic of a parallel circuit is that all components are connected between the same set of electrically common points.

pool.q: In a parallel circuit, what is true about voltage?
options: It is zero across each branch
It is equal across all components
It increases with each branch added
pool.explain: There are only two sets of electrically common points, so every branch sees the same voltage.
pool.evidence: The first principle to understand about parallel circuits is that the voltage is equal across all components in the circuit.

pool.q: Which rule applies to the variables in an Ohm's Law equation?
options: They must come from different components
Voltage must always be the largest
They must all refer to the same two points in the circuit
pool.explain: Mixing contexts is a common beginner's mistake.
pool.evidence: The variables used in Ohm's Law equations must be common to the same two points in the circuit under consideration.

pool.q: How are the holes on a solderless breadboard connected?
options: Every hole connects to every other
pool.explain: Metal spring clips under the face join each group.
pool.evidence: unlike the holes on a solderless breadboard which are connected together in groups of five

pool.q: In a series circuit, what determines how voltage drops are proportioned?
pool.explain: That is why the voltage divider formula works.
pool.evidence: The proportionality of voltage drops (ratio of one to another) is strictly a function of resistance values.

pool.q: What is a potentiometer?
options: A resistor with a movable element set by a knob or lever
pool.explain: It is often used as an adjustable voltage divider.
pool.evidence: which is a resistor with a movable element positioned by a manual knob or lever

pool.q: What does Kirchhoff's Voltage Law state?
options: Current into a node equals current out
The algebraic sum of all voltages in a loop equals zero
pool.explain: A loop is any path that returns to its starting point.
pool.evidence: The algebraic sum of all voltages in a loop must equal zero

pool.q: In Kirchhoff's Voltage Law, what does 'algebraic' mean?
options: Accounting for signs (polarities) as well as magnitudes
pool.explain: Voltage rises and drops cancel out around the loop.
pool.evidence: I mean accounting for signs (polarities) as well as magnitudes

pool.q: What does Kirchhoff's Current Law say about a node?
options: All current stops at a node
The current entering it equals the current leaving it
pool.explain: Like a pipe fitting with no leaks: what flows in must flow out.
pool.evidence: the current entering the node is equal in magnitude to the current exiting the node

pool.q: In a parallel circuit, how does total current relate to branch currents?
options: It equals the sum of the branch currents
It equals the smallest branch current
It equals the average branch current
It is unrelated to the branches
pool.explain: This follows directly from Kirchhoff's Current Law.
pool.evidence: We know that the total current in a parallel circuit must equal the sum of the branch currents
